title: A Graph That Looks After Itself: Watching Nodes, Restarting the One That Stalls, and Stopping Safely When That Fails

questions.question: The sensor in a running graph stops producing, and stays active. What stops the arm acting on stale data first?
options: The supervisor, which restarts the sensor at 5.17 s before any stale command is sent
The launcher, which takes the graph down when the sensor stalls
The controller's own watchdog, a deadline of 0.2 s that commands a stop once: it acted at 5.12 s, before the supervisor at 5.17 s
The sensor's own lifecycle state, which changes to inactive when it stalls
questions.explanation: The controller does not wait to be told. With no plan for 0.2 s it commands a stop by itself, and the supervisor's repair comes after.

questions.question: Why is the supervisor's detection a deadline after the last scan and not after the stall?
options: Nobody knows when a silence begins until the next output fails to come: the last scan was at 4.91 s and it was seen at 5.17 s
The supervisor polls only once a second
The sensor reports its own stall after a delay
The clock of the supervisor runs behind the sensor's
questions.explanation: A silence is only known once an expected output has failed to arrive. So the deadline of 0.25 s runs from the last scan, at 4.91 s.

questions.question: The sensor stalls and the viewer fed from it goes quiet too. What should the supervisor do with the viewer?
options: Restart it, since it missed its deadline like the sensor
Give up on it at once, since it is optional
Shut it down until the sensor is back, then start it again
Report it starved and leave it alone with a fresh deadline: restarting the victims leaves the fault where it was
questions.explanation: The viewer is silent because nothing reaches it. It is told which nodes it listens to, so the supervisor marks it starved and repairs only the cause.

questions.question: A restart fails because the device cannot be opened. What happens next?
options: It is retried at once, as fast as the supervisor can loop
The node gets a fresh deadline and is noticed stalled again 0.26 s later: restart failed, stalled, restart failed, stalled, gave up, 0.69 s after the stall
The supervisor gives up at the first failed restart
The node is left stalled and never looked at again
questions.explanation: A failed restart is reported and the node is watched again. Two restarts are allowed, so the third stall, 0.69 s after the first, is a give up.

questions.question: An optional viewer is given up on. What happens to the graph?
options: It is taken down in reverse order, as for any give up
It is paused until an operator confirms
The controller's watchdog stops the arm
It carries on: gave_up() stays false and the arm got 49 move commands in 5 s with no stops
questions.explanation: The viewer is a convenience. The supervisor tried once and gave up on it, and the rest of the graph was untouched.

questions.question: What does a restart give the node, besides the new life cycle?
options: A new incarnation number, which the supervisor waits for
A longer deadline than before
A fresh deadline, so it is not reported again at once: one stall in 6 s gave 1 stalled event and 1 restart
Nothing more: it is watched exactly as before
questions.explanation: Without a fresh deadline the node would be reported stalled again at the very next look, before it had had time to produce anything.
